placements.why: The entire document concerns instrument calibration — establishing it, verifying it against reference plates, and recording it as a key decision. Calibration is an organizational category that future envelopes may feed, and nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers it.
placements.title: Calibration
placements.frame: What calibration activities are performed, how are they verified, and how are they recorded as settled?

placements.title: From unverified to calibrated and verified against reference standards
placements.frame: How is an instrument brought to a calibrated state, verified against reference artifacts, and recorded as settled?
placements.why: All three expressions concern the same calibration fact: src-1 asserts the Kestrelwood spectrograph is calibrated at 88.4 MHz, src-2 claims verification against June reference plates across the full observing band, and src-3 records it as a key decision. Calibration verification is a recurring activity future envelopes will keep feeding — this is a thematic subject, not a one-time fact. No existing leaf plausibly holds this theme.
